# WHAT IT IS FOR. gates.sh builds its gate list by globbing gates/regress/*.js, so it counts the gates it FINDS.
# A gate that was deleted, renamed, or never merged is therefore indistinguishable from a gate that was never
# needed, and the suite still ends "GATES GREEN". Measured at #450 and again here: gates/regress/67-sel-cls-
# consumers.js, the only gate that reddens on the sel/cls consumer P0s, is absent from main, and
# gates/regress/50-drill-verdict-no-jump.js was authored 2026-09-22 for the drill board jump and committed by
# nobody. Main's suite reported 47 suites green with both of them missing and no tool in this project said so.
# HOW IT IS READ. gates/gatemanifest.sh check compares this file against gates/regress/ on disk:
#   state=required  MUST be on disk. Absent  -> gates.sh FAILS BEFORE RUNNING ANY GATE and cannot emit GATES GREEN.
#   state=absent    known to exist somewhere and NOT on main. Reported loudly on every run; does NOT redden.
#   state=retired   deliberately removed. The row STAYS - see "a row is never deleted" below. Does not redden.
#   no row at all   UNLISTED: the suite still runs (a new gate must be able to), but the footer records it and
#                   gates/verify-log.sh REFUSES the log, so a gate cannot reach main without a row here.
# A ROW IS NEVER DELETED, which is the whole mechanism and is borrowed from gates/build-numbers.tsv. To remove a
# gate you run `gates/gatemanifest.sh retire <gate> '<why>'`, which flips state to retired and writes the reason
# INTO THIS FILE, so the removal appears in a commit diff with its justification attached. Deleting the row
# instead would make the manifest agree with the deletion silently, which is the defect this file exists to stop.
# WHY required IS NOT "EVERY GATE THAT HAS EVER EXISTED" [CLAUDE.md, #405, the frozen denominator]. The 47
# required rows below are seeded from the committed suite at #461 and nothing else. THEIR PROVENANCE, STATED
# HONESTLY RATHER THAN INVENTED: the build and date columns read 461 / 2026-10-02 for all 47 because that is when
# the ROW was written, NOT when the gate was introduced - those build numbers are recoverable from git log and are
# deliberately not guessed here. The `covers` column is each gate's own header comment, truncated, not a fresh
# fields: gate <TAB> state <TAB> build <TAB> at <TAB> who <TAB> covers <TAB> note
